name: Sandeep Hotel & Restaurant
why_it_matters: A bus-stand-side family-run hotel with a working dhaba kitchen — the place locals point Char Dham travellers to when they want a hot meal at minimal cost. Owner Sandeep speaks English; thalis change with what's fresh that morning.
insider_tip: Order the Garhwali thali rather than the standard north-Indian menu — it's the kitchen's strong suit and includes the seasonal pahadi sabzi that doesn't make it onto the printed card.
signature_address: Main Market, Malyasu Malla, Rudraprayag, Uttarakhand 246171

name: GMVN Rudra Tourist Complex Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Uttarakhand state tourism corporation's (Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam) own dining hall, run inside the Rudra Tourist Complex overlooking the Mandakini-Alaknanda confluence. Standard-issue government-canteen menu, but the terrace view is the reason to come.
insider_tip: Open to walk-ins, not just resident guests — ask for a table on the riverside terrace. Breakfast (7-9am) is the most reliable meal; lunch waits can stretch when Char Dham buses pull in.
signature_address: GMVN Rudra Tourist Complex, Rudraprayag, Uttarakhand 246171

name: Monal Resort Restaurant
why_it_matters: An open-air restaurant inside one of Rudraprayag's longest-running mid-market resorts (operating ~25 years). The lawns sit above the Alaknanda; the kitchen serves the standard Char Dham-route veg/non-veg menu with consistency that other highway hotels don't match.
insider_tip: About 3-4km from town centre on the Badrinath highway — useful if you're driving through and want a sit-down meal without entering Rudraprayag's narrow bazaar lanes. Lawn seating only works in clear weather; the indoor section is small.

name: Hotel Bhanu Palace Restaurant
why_it_matters: One of the few hotel kitchens in Rudraprayag that explicitly markets a Garhwali section — mandua (finger millet) roti, pahadi raita, gundruk — alongside the standard north-Indian and Chinese menu. 24-hour kitchen, useful for late Kedarnath-route arrivals.
insider_tip: Ask for the local thali rather than the generic veg one. Open round the clock, but Garhwali items run out by mid-evening — order before 8pm if mandua roti is the reason you came.

name: Alaknanda Motel & Restaurant
why_it_matters: A purpose-built motel-restaurant on the Badrinath highway (Sumerpur side of Rudraprayag) — set up for Char Dham road traffic. Breakfast is à la carte rather than buffet, with vegan and special-diet options that other highway stops don't carry.
insider_tip: If you're a long-haul driver, this is one of the few places where the kitchen will actually do an off-menu request — call ahead on +91-9999101637 if you need an early start before sunrise.
signature_address: Sumerpur, Badrinath Highway, Rudraprayag District, Uttarakhand 246171

name: Hotel Suri Restaurant
why_it_matters: A 15-room budget hotel on the Badrinath highway, 1 km from the main bus stand and 2 km from the Sangam — the dining hall is geared for Char Dham yatris on a tight timetable. Standard veg-only fare, room-service available.
insider_tip: Walk-in meals are accepted but the kitchen prioritises hotel guests at lunch (12-2pm) and dinner (8-9:30pm); aim for the gap between if you're not staying. Rooms start at ₹999 if the eatery and a bed for the night are both options.

name: Sardar Ji Pakode Wale
signature_dish: mix pakora with green-chilli mint chutney
why_it_matters: A roadside shack on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway at Nagrasu (~18km north of Rudraprayag), run by a Sikh family. The pakoras are double-fried — partially fried first, then re-fried — which is why every Char Dham travel blog notes the crispness. Mix plate is ₹80.
insider_tip: It's a stand-up stall, not a restaurant — pull over, eat off the steel plate, drink the chai out of a glass, get back on the road. Open 7am-7:30pm; queues form after 4pm when buses heading down from Kedarnath stop here.
signature_address: Badrinath Road, Nagrasu, Rudraprayag District, Uttarakhand 246171
